step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard shows six components: a fire hydrant (IoT edge device), API Gateway, S3, ECS, SageMaker and an Analyst. All are kept as nodes; the analyst is kept because it is an endpoint of ledger connections and an active participant in the classification and feedback loop. No fusion or expansion is needed, since each service appears once and the audio names no additional services. Flow 0 is the daily ingestion and leak detection pipeline: hydrants push correlated acoustic files through API Gateway (authentication and security), files are persisted in S3, a daily batch process in ECS processes the files as node pairs to find correlations and persistent correlations, ECS calls a SageMaker ML endpoint to assign a leak probability, and the leak score is fed to the human analysts. Flow 1 is the feedback loop: field feedback is used about every six weeks to further classify and retrain the model (Analyst -> SageMaker, meta). Self-check: the visual_connections ledger has 6 entries and 6 edges are emitted, one per entry with the same source and target, including both directions between SageMaker and the Analyst.

graph.name: Mueller Water Products: Water Intelligence Platform for Acoustic Leak Detection
graph.notes: Water intelligence platform that ingests data from a large-scale IoT network of meters, smart fire hydrants, pressure monitoring and water quality devices. Acoustic data from fire hydrants is ingested daily, batch processed for correlations, and scored by an ML model for leak probability so human analysts can focus on the most important noise sources. Benefits: reduction of non-revenue water loss and ecological protection. Future: heavier focus on ML and analytics, plus additional data sources such as flow and pressure.

nodes.name: Smart Fire Hydrant
nodes.notes: IoT fire hydrants that record acoustic signals measuring noises on the pipe network. Signals are recorded daily and correlated between multiple fire hydrants.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Entry point for the daily acoustic files. Provides authentication and security; chosen instead of writing directly to S3 because of the heavy focus on IoT security.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Persists the acoustic files pushed through API Gateway.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Container microservices running a daily batch process in which each file is processed as a node pair to look for correlations in the acoustic signals, including persistent correlations that occur over many days. Chosen over Lambda because the acoustic algorithms are very processor intensive.

nodes.name: SageMaker ML Endpoint
nodes.notes: ML endpoint that further classifies persistent correlations and assigns a leak probability (leak score). The model is retrained about every six weeks using feedback from the field.

nodes.name: Analyst
nodes.notes: Human analyst team that receives the leak score, reviews the persistent correlation, checks with the water utility for other nearby noise sources, and updates the leak status to field investigation required.

edges.notes: Correlated acoustic signal files are pushed through API Gateway on a daily basis.
After authentication and security checks, the files are pushed and persisted in S3.
A daily batch process in ECS processes each file as a node pair to look for correlations in the acoustic signals.
Persistent correlations are sent to the SageMaker ML endpoint to be classified and assigned a leak probability.
The leak score (probability) is fed to the human analyst team, who further classify the leak.
Feedback from the field is used about every six weeks to further classify and retrain the model, so it improves over time.
